purpose: Reproducible primary-source ground truth for JEFF protocol evaluation and calibration policy.

decisionRules.rule: Use the canonical ownerless singleton registry and verify the implementation, salt, chain ID, token contract, and token ID before trusting an account address.
A canonical account address can be computed before deployment, but the selected implementation remains part of the trust boundary.
Resolve control from the NFT on the chain named by the account, not from an assumed local-chain holder.
Do not assume one NFT has exactly one token-bound account because different implementations and salts are valid.
Reject ownership cycles because they can permanently lock assets.
Accept valueDecimals only in the inclusive range 0 through 18.
Reject feedback submitted by the agent owner or operator.
Treat registration and advertised capabilities as claims, not proof that an agent is safe or functional.
Keep identity, reputation, and validation evidence distinct and scale the trust model to value at risk.
Do not treat raw reputation count as independent evidence without Sybil analysis.
Bind signatures to the current chain ID and EntryPoint.
Run the complete validation simulation and drop a UserOperation when validation reverts or fails.
Require the operation validity interval to contain the current time.
Require sufficient paymaster deposit and treat returned context as a requirement to run postOp.
Apply ERC-7562 validation-scope and reputation rules to shared mempool admission.

protocolSources.title: Standard Signature Validation Method for Contracts

decisionRules.rule: Accept a contract signature only when isValidSignature returns exactly 0x1626ba7e.
Call signature validation with STATICCALL because validation must not modify state.
Revalidate against current contract state and context because validity can change over time.
Treat revert, malformed return data, and every non-magic return value as invalid.
Require sequence to equal current sequence plus one and prevStateRoot to equal the current state root.
Never place raw memory, salts, keys, or raw locators in calldata.
Reject registries whose enforcing logic or upgrade authority can change after deployment.
Bind EIP-712 authorization to the chain and registry contract.
Protect low-entropy commitments with encryption or a secret salt because public salts permit targeted guessing.
Do not infer authorization from EIP-7702 code presence alone.
Enforce the exact job state transitions and caller roles for open, fund, submit, complete, reject, and expire.
Require a nonzero evaluator and treat evaluator selection as an explicit trust decision.
Do not allow the client to unilaterally withdraw a funded job outside the specified terminal paths.
Treat hooks as trusted code, bound their gas, audit or allowlist them, and reject upgradeable hooks for high-value use.
Use safe token transfer handling and reentrancy protection around settlement.
Apply opcode, code, storage, stake, and reputation constraints before admitting shared-mempool UserOperations.

protocolSources.title: Secure Protocol for Native Meta Transactions

decisionRules.rule: Accept an appended signer only from a recipient-approved trusted forwarder that verifies signatures and nonces.

protocolSources.title: Typed structured data hashing and signing

decisionRules.rule: Add application-level nonce or idempotency checks because EIP-712 does not itself provide replay protection.
Verify domain chainId and verifyingContract and refuse a mismatched signing domain.
Resolve and validate the delegated implementation; code presence alone does not prove current authority or safe behavior.
